grades.quote: The machine level has the highest privileges and is the only mandatory privilege level for a RISC-V hardware platform. Code run in machine-mode (M-mode) is usually inherently trusted, as it has lowlevel access to the machine implementation. M-mode can be used to manage secure execution environments on RISC-V. User-mode (U-mode) and supervisor-mode (S-mode) are intended for conventional application and operating system usage respectively.
grades.reason: Directly explains M-mode's privileged machine access and the intended application and operating-system roles of U-mode and S-mode.
Security research exercises do not explain RISC-V privilege modes.
